findings.title: Server record-creation time (Evidence.capturedAtUtc = server now() at reserve/upload) is presented as capture time, and public Basic Verify says it was 'declared by the capturing device'
findings.userImpact: Reviewers read a server bookkeeping time as the moment the material was captured. For uploads and intake there is no capturing device at all; for the extension the value is when the session was reserved, after the capture ran.
findings.legalImpact: Public Verify makes a false provenance statement (attributing a server timestamp to the device); reports/Verify give a 'Captured At' time that is neither the capture time nor labelled as server receipt, which can be relied on for timeline arguments.
findings.reproduction: Upload any file via POST /v1/evidence (or capture a page with the extension). createEvidence sets capturedAtUtc = new Date() (evidence.service.ts:446, written at :531). GET /public/verify/:id in BASIC mode -> buildBasicVerification copies it to original.capturedAtUtcDeclared (basic-verification.ts:253), rendered 'Captured (declared by the capturing device): <server time>' (BasicVerificationView.tsx:216). Full Verify renders it under 'Captured At' (page.tsx:4098); the report exec grid renders it under 'Captured & Signed' (executive-summary.ts:356-360 via build-view-model.ts:365); evidence detail 'Captured at' (EvidenceIntegrityTab.tsx:378). For the extension, background.ts captures at :46-52 and only then opens (:55) and reserves (:59), so 'Captured from the web at (server UTC)' (evidence-acquisition.ts:454) is post-capture reservation time.
findings.observed: One server clock value (record creation) is labelled 'declared by the capturing device', 'Captured At', 'Captured & Signed', 'Captured at'. The API already knows better: it emits capturedAtUtcLabel 'Server-recorded intake time' / capturedAtUtcProvenance 'server_clock' (evidence.routes.ts:5054-5055), which the UI drops. The report Capture Context row labelled '(server UTC)' falls back to deviceTimeIso (client clock) when capturedAtUtc is null (build-view-model.ts:1654-1658); Verify's 'Capture timestamp' does the same (page.tsx:3658-3663). The actual client capture window (manifest captureStartedAtUtc/EndedAtUtc) is never projected.
findings.expected: Label the value as what it is ('Recorded by PROOVRA (server UTC)' / 'Record created'); never attribute it to a device; show client-reported capture window (manifest) separately and labelled client-reported; never mix server and device clocks under one label.
findings.rootCause: The column is named capturedAtUtc but holds server creation time; surfaces label it by its name, and basic-verification.ts invented a 'Declared' semantics for it.
findings.remediation: Rename the projection field (e.g. recordedAtUtc) in BasicVerification (keep old key as alias), relabel all listed surfaces to server-receipt wording, surface manifest captureStartedAtUtc as 'Capture started (reported by client)', and remove the deviceTimeIso fallback under server-UTC labels.
findings.requiredTests: Render tests for BasicVerificationView / mobile basic view / Verify summary / report exec grid asserting no 'Captured' or 'declared by device' wording for capturedAtUtc; unit test that basic-verification output does not claim device origin.
findings.runtimeProbe: Create a web upload on a disposable DB, publish it, GET /public/verify/:id?basic and assert original.capturedAtUtcDeclared equals evidence.created_at-time server clock (proving it is not device-declared).

findings.title: Every direct-capture record (extension, Android screen, continuous, iOS) reads 'Capture Method: Not recorded' in report, package, custody presentation and Verify technical metadata, contradicting the acquisition statement in the same artifact
findings.userImpact: A reviewer sees 'Web capture - PROOVRA extension (client-attested)' in the acquisition panel and 'Capture Method: Not recorded' a few rows later; the package's case-metadata.json and court-admissibility-checklist.json say 'Not recorded' while acquisition.json names the mode.
findings.legalImpact: Internally inconsistent provenance statements in a forensic export undermine the record; a direct capture is downgraded to 'not recorded' on the fields most reviewers read.
findings.reproduction: captureMethodDisplayLabel switches only SECURE_INTAKE_LINK / PROOVRA_WEB_UPLOAD / PROOVRA_MOBILE_APP and returns 'Not recorded' for DIRECT_WEB_CAPTURE_EXTENSION, DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_ANDROID(_CONTINUOUS), DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_IOS (display-helpers.ts:38-45). acquisition.ts mapMethod does the same (:155-162) so buildEvidenceAcquisitionContext returns null for them (:235). Generate a report/package for a sealed extension capture: technical-model 'Capture Method' (:251), build-view-model (:690), truth-model canonical materials (:383), package case-metadata/court checklist/canonical-record (verification-package.ts:1250/1265/2366), custody presentationPayload (normalizers.ts:59) all say 'Not recorded'.
findings.observed: 'Not recorded' for four recorded acquisition modes.
findings.expected: Derive the label from resolveEvidenceAcquisition(...).label (or an explicit case per mode) so every surface names the same mode.
findings.rootCause: Two hand-maintained switch tables in shared-runtime were not widened when UC-1..UC-5 added modes; resolveEvidenceAcquisition is not their source.
findings.remediation: Make captureMethodDisplayLabel and mapMethod exhaustive over EvidenceAcquisitionMode (compile-time exhaustiveness via Record<EvidenceAcquisitionMode,string>), defaulting to the descriptor label.
findings.requiredTests: Exhaustiveness test iterating EVIDENCE_ACQUISITION_MODES asserting no mode except LEGACY_NOT_RECORDED maps to 'Not recorded'; package fixture for a direct capture asserting case-metadata.captureMethod == acquisition.json label.

findings.title: Web/screen capture manifest facts (source URL, title, browser, extension/app version, client capture window, completeness, page-mutated flag, detected limitation codes) are validated then dropped; no surface can state them
findings.userImpact: A web capture record never shows which URL/page was captured, and a PARTIAL capture or one with PAGE_MUTATED_DURING_CAPTURE / CROSS_ORIGIN_IFRAME_NOT_CAPTURED is presented identically to a complete one; likewise FLAG_SECURE omissions on Android frames.
findings.legalImpact: WEB_PAGE_STATE_AT_CAPTURE text and the legal page promise PROOVRA records 'any limitations it detected' and 'the page URL captured'; neither is surfaced, so a reviewer cannot see detected completeness defects except by hand-parsing the raw capture-manifest.json in a package.
findings.reproduction: Grep for readers of sourceUrlPrivate / pageMutatedDuringCapture / extensionVersion / captureStartedAtUtc / WebCaptureLimitationCode outside the validator and extension: none in services/api, services/worker, apps/web, packages/shared-runtime. completeWebCaptureSession uses the parsed manifest only for digest cross-check (web-capture.service.ts:77-116) and then relabels the part (:131-134). Report, Verify, evidence detail and search have no projection of it; the package ships the raw bytes as a CAPTURE_MANIFEST part only.
findings.observed: Manifest facts exist only inside an opaque JSON part.
findings.expected: A bounded server-side projection (private: sourceUrl; public: domain; all: completeness, detected limitation codes, browser/app version, client-reported capture window) persisted at seal and rendered with 'reported by the capture client' labelling; detected limitations appended to the acquisition limitation list.
findings.rootCause: UC-1/UC-2 stopped at validation; no projection/persistence step for manifest facts was built.
findings.remediation: At seal, persist a validated manifest summary (e.g. evidence.captureManifestSummary JSON or a table) and surface it in report/Verify/detail/package; add a PARTIAL/mutated banner.
findings.requiredTests: Seal a web capture with completeness PARTIAL and PAGE_MUTATED_DURING_CAPTURE; assert report, Verify and detail show both; assert public Verify shows domain only.

findings.title: Direct Web Capture legal page and in-app capture card still claim the session opens before capture, PROOVRA 'participates'/'takes part' in the capture and 'produces the bytes', and that the server establishes capture time
findings.userImpact: Users and reviewers are told the capture is server-participating; code captures first and opens the session afterwards, and the server observes nothing but uploaded bytes.
findings.legalImpact: Upgrades a client-attested capture to a server-participating one in the published 'how it works' disclosure relied on by legal reviewers; contradicts the product's own limitation CAPTURE_CLIENT_ATTESTED.
findings.reproduction: Read /settings/legal/direct-web-capture: 'the extension opens a server-issued capture session before the capture begins' (md:17), 'PROOVRA participates in the capture' (md:18), 'PROOVRA's own capture adapter produces the bytes under a session that the server issued in advance' (md:21), 'the capture timestamp (the server establishes the authoritative time)' (md:28). Capture card: 'PROOVRA takes part in the capture ... records how and when the page was captured' (CaptureDirectWebCaptureCard.tsx:64-68). background.ts captures at :46-52, opens the session at :55.
findings.observed: Pre-ET-DC-02/03 wording survives in the legal corpus and the capture card although the descriptors were reworded.
findings.expected: Same wording as the descriptor: the extension reports it captured the page; session opened after capture; server recomputed digests; time shown is server receipt.
findings.rootCause: ET-DC-02/03 remediation reworded evidence-acquisition.ts only; copy outside the resolver was not swept.
findings.remediation: Rewrite the four legal sentences and the capture-card body; regenerate corpus.generated.ts; add a copy guard test banning 'participates in the capture', 'before the capture begins', 'takes part in the capture'.
findings.requiredTests: Corpus/copy guard test over apps/web/content/legal and capture card.

findings.title: Report 'Capture Device' block presents the uploading browser's User-Agent OS/device/browser and a client-supplied timezone as the capture device, next to EXIF camera
findings.userImpact: A phone photo uploaded from a Windows desktop reads 'Capture Device: <EXIF camera> / Operating system: Windows / Device: Desktop / Timezone: <browser tz>'.
findings.legalImpact: Upload environment is upgraded to capture environment; timezone is a request-body value with no provenance label.
findings.reproduction: POST /v1/evidence from any browser with captureTimezone in body: recordCaptureEnvironment stores UA-derived os/device/browser and body.captureTimezone (evidence.routes.ts:5594-5611). technical-summary.ts:116-145 renders them in renderGroup('Capture Device') with the EXIF camera; executive-summary.ts:84-98 renders the same rows unlabelled in the summary grid.
findings.observed: Upload-request environment labelled as capture device.
findings.expected: Group titled 'Submission environment (uploading browser, as reported by its User-Agent)'; timezone labelled client-reported; keep EXIF camera under its own file-embedded heading.
findings.rootCause: Capture Environment was designed for in-browser capture and reused unchanged for uploads.
findings.remediation: Rename the group and rows; add provenance labels (server-observed UA header vs client-reported timezone).
findings.requiredTests: Report render test for an upload with EXIF asserting the UA rows are not under 'Capture Device'.

findings.title: Intake 'identityVerification' / 'submissionType' are derived from the link creator's identity snapshot and emitted on public Verify JSON as the contributor's ('Verified', 'Organization User')
findings.userImpact: Not rendered by current web/mobile UI, but public API consumers and the unrendered report executiveRows 'Contributor Identity' receive 'Verified' for an unverified remote contributor whenever the link creator's email is verified.
findings.legalImpact: Link creator's verified identity -> contributor 'Verified' in a public machine-readable response.
findings.reproduction: Intake evidence is created with ownerUserId = link.createdByUserId (external-intake-orchestration.service.ts:321-322); identityLevelSnapshot is computed from that owner (evidence.service.ts:458-467). verify-projection reads e.identity_level_snapshot (:383) into buildEvidenceAcquisitionContext; mapIdentityVerification maps VERIFIED_EMAIL -> 'Verified' (acquisition.ts:170-172) and toPublicAcquisition includes it in the public projection (:342-345). technical-model.ts:189-196 already documents this value is requester-derived.
findings.observed: Requester identity projected as contributor verification in public JSON and in vm.executiveRows.
findings.expected: For intake, identityVerification = 'Not independently verified' regardless of the requester snapshot.
findings.rootCause: ET-INT-12 fix relabelled rendered surfaces but left the shared mapper keyed on the owner snapshot.
findings.remediation: In buildEvidenceAcquisitionContext return the fixed contributor label when isIntake; drop build-view-model.ts:372 or feed it the fixed label.
findings.requiredTests: Unit: intake + VERIFIED_EMAIL identityLevel -> identityVerification 'Not independently verified'.

findings.title: Verification package ships 'court-admissibility-checklist.json' with packetProfile 'COURT_READY_SUPPORTING_PACKET', a phrase the product's own forbidden-phrase list bans
findings.userImpact: Recipients see 'court-ready' framing on every package regardless of acquisition tier.
findings.legalImpact: Implies legal status; mitigated by remainingHumanRequirements text.
findings.reproduction: Build any package: buildCourtReadinessChecklist returns packetProfile 'COURT_READY_SUPPORTING_PACKET' (:2329), filed as court-admissibility-checklist.json (:523); FORBIDDEN_ARTIFACT_PHRASES lists 'court-ready' (report-artifact.ts:173).
findings.observed: Court-ready naming in a forensic export.
findings.expected: Neutral naming (e.g. reviewer-readiness-checklist.json, profile 'SUPPORTING_REVIEW_PACKET'), keeping a legacy alias if external tools depend on it.
findings.rootCause: Forbidden-phrase guard applies to report artifact copy, not package file names/profile values.
findings.remediation: Rename profile/file; extend the forbidden-phrase guard to package entry names and JSON string values.
findings.requiredTests: Package guard test scanning entry names and JSON values for FORBIDDEN_ARTIFACT_PHRASES.

findings.title: captureMethod structure enum still reaches exports as an origin label: exchange-package metadata.json 'captureMethod: UPLOADED_FILE' with no acquisitionMode, package file names built from it, plus dead 'Captured with PROOVRA secure camera' mappers
findings.userImpact: A direct screen/web capture transferred via exchange package is described as captureMethod UPLOADED_FILE / MULTIPART_PACKAGE; package file names embed 'uploaded_file-image'.
findings.legalImpact: Structure read as origin (downgrade) in an inter-organization transfer artifact; the acquisition authority is absent from it.
findings.reproduction: exchange-package-builder.ts:384 writes ev.captureMethod raw into evidence/<id>/metadata.json. processor.ts:1809-1832 derives UPLOADED_FILE/IMPORTED_DOCUMENT/MULTIPART_PACKAGE from item count/MIME and passes it as metadata.captureMethod (:4755) into buildEvidencePackageFileName -> deriveEvidenceDescriptor (verification-package.ts:474-477). getCaptureMethodLabel (no callers) and normalizeReviewerText keep SECURE_CAMERA -> 'PROOVRA secure camera' mappings though no production writer emits SECURE_CAMERA (only seed scripts).
findings.observed: Structure field presented as capture method in exports; upgrade copy retained in dead/latent mappers.
findings.expected: Exports carry acquisitionMode + label (resolveEvidenceAcquisition) and name structure 'evidenceStructure'; remove SECURE_CAMERA 'secure camera' copy.
findings.rootCause: UC-0 sweep covered report/Verify/package JSON labels but not the exchange builder, file naming, or legacy mappers.
findings.remediation: Add acquisition to exchange metadata.json and rename captureMethod->evidenceStructure; drop captureMethod from file naming; delete getCaptureMethodLabel and the SECURE_CAMERA replacement.
findings.requiredTests: Exchange package fixture for a DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_ANDROID record asserts acquisition.mode present and no 'captureMethod' origin field.

findings.title: Set-once trigger allows NULL -> (any mode, 'RECORDED_AT_CREATION') on UPDATE, so a legacy record can later be given a contemporaneous-looking acquisition
findings.userImpact: none today (no app writer); defense-in-depth gap for operators/scripts.
findings.legalImpact: Contradicts the stated invariant that a backfill 'can never pass for a contemporaneous record'.
findings.securityImpact: Privileged DB writer could retro-label legacy evidence as a direct capture recorded at creation.
findings.reproduction: UPDATE evidence SET acquisition_mode='DIRECT_WEB_CAPTURE_EXTENSION', acquisition_mode_source='RECORDED_AT_CREATION' WHERE acquisition_mode IS NULL; — trigger branches only fire when OLD value IS NOT NULL (migration.sql:132-143); CHECKs pass.
findings.expected: On UPDATE, refuse NEW.acquisition_mode_source = 'RECORDED_AT_CREATION' when OLD.acquisition_mode IS NULL (only backfill sources may be set later).
findings.rootCause: Trigger designed to permit the D9 backfill but not constrained to backfill sources.
findings.remediation: Additive CREATE OR REPLACE of the trigger function adding the NULL->RECORDED_AT_CREATION refusal.
findings.requiredTests: PG integration test: NULL row update to RECORDED_AT_CREATION raises check_violation; BACKFILL_* allowed.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable PG16: insert evidence with NULL mode, run the UPDATE above, expect success today (proves gap).

findings.title: Mobile continuous capture shows client-computed 'Complete — no known interruption' with the 'verified' badge tone
findings.userImpact: Completeness asserted by the app is styled as a verification success.
findings.legalImpact: Minor: client-asserted continuity visually upgraded to verified.
findings.reproduction: Finish a continuous recording without interruption; review card renders ProovraBadge tone='verified' (continuous-capture.tsx:451-454).
findings.observed: Verified tone for a client claim.
findings.expected: Neutral tone; 'reported complete by this device'.
findings.rootCause: Tone chosen for positive state rather than evidentiary basis.
findings.remediation: Use neutral tone and client-reported wording.

findings.title: Capture page trust strip claims 'End-to-end protected' although bytes are uploaded in clear to PROOVRA storage and hashed server-side
findings.userImpact: Overstates confidentiality model (server can read content).
findings.legalImpact: Security-property upgrade: TLS + storage encryption presented as end-to-end.
findings.securityImpact: Misleading security claim; no technical exposure.
findings.reproduction: Open /capture; strip item 'End-to-end protected — Encrypted storage and verifiable audit trail' (CaptureTrustStrip.tsx:31-33). Server recomputes SHA-256 of stored plaintext at completion (evidence-complete path), which E2E would preclude.
findings.remediation: Reword; add to capture copy guard.
